title: Tenant burst protection and retry-amplification fix for hosted API
creator: Amir Patel
description: Summary: Multiple paying customers reported recurring 5xx bursts and long tail timeouts during peak traffic windows. Investigations indicated tenant-local retry amplification and uneven connection pool distribution triggered by a malformed per-tenant backoff policy and an edge-case in KV cache eviction, leading to head-of-line stalls on inference workers. This ticket coordinates short-term mitigations, a targeted code fix, and customer communications to resolve escalations.
actions: Short-term mitigations: 1) Roll out per-tenant soft rate limit (100 rps default) via the routing layer to reduce instantaneous amplification. 2) Apply a conservative global client-side retry cap (max 2 retries) in the hosted API SDKs and gateway to prevent exponential retry storms. 3) Temporarily route high-error tenants to a compatible, lower-throughput model variant to preserve availability. 4) Increase connection pool size on worker pools for tenant-heavy partitions where CPU was saturating. Codefix: Fix race in KV cache eviction that could cause stale pointer dereference under concurrent writes; add per-tenant cache lock and stronger invariant checks. Long-term: Implement adaptive retry orchestration (server signals to clients to reduce retries), tenant-exposure dashboards, and automated canary throttles on surge detection.
acceptance_criteria: 1) No customer-reported repeat 5xx waves for 48 hours after rollout. 2) Dashboard shows queue depth and error rate per-tenant decreased by >=80% during comparable traffic. 3) Integration test exercising concurrent KV cache writes passes consistently under high concurrency. 4) SDK default retry cap shipped and documented.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (hotfix): Deploy rate-limit config to routing layer in staged regions (us-east-1 -> eu-west-1) with shadow metrics for 30 minutes, then enable enforcement. Patch worker pools and increase pool size via infra flag. Phase 2 (code): Deploy KV cache patch behind feature flag, run extended canary against low-traffic tenants for 6 hours, then promote. Phase 3 (clients): Release SDK minor that caps retries and surfaces server backoff headers. Communication: Send status updates to affected customers after Phase 1 and post-incident summary after full rollout.

postmortem_summary: Root cause: combined effects of an over-aggressive client retry pattern, missing server-side retry coordination, and a GC-time-induced race in KV cache eviction. Immediate mitigation (per-tenant soft limits + SDK retry cap) restored customer availability. Long-term changes include adaptive retry orchestration, stronger cache invariants, and tenant surge observability. Action items assigned and scheduled for the next two cycles.
next_steps: 1) Merge KV cache patch after adding concurrent tests (Sasha). 2) Promote worker pool sizing change to remaining regions (SRE). 3) Ship SDK minor release and notify customers (SDK + Developer Experience). 4) Add tenant surge alerts and automated throttle playbooks to Console (Product + Observability).
